description: The RN-safe device side: src/agent-client/AgentClient.ts plus the AITab wiring and barrel exports. AgentClient pairs over POST /pair, opens the WS with the RN global WebSocket, exposes ask(question, conversation, {onToken, onPatch}), and ANSWERS inbound device-side tool_calls (get_network_logs/get_console_logs) from AppLens.getStorage(). AITab probes aiAgentURL on mount: reachable routes handleSend through AgentClient and streams via the existing buffer/scheduleFlush and renders a read-only diff bubble; unreachable/unset keeps today's exact behavior (no regression). Only AgentClient and the shared protocol TYPES are re-exported from src/index.ts — nothing else from src/agent. Depends on FEAT-001 for protocol.ts types and the running server contract; this closes the runtime-log round-trip whose agent-side half shipped in FEAT-001.
steps: Create src/agent-client/AgentClient.ts (RN-safe; use the RN global WebSocket, NOT the `ws` package; import only shared protocol TYPES from src/agent/protocol, no other src/agent import). Methods: constructor(baseURL); pair() -> POST /pair returning {token,wsUrl}; connect() opens the WS presenting the token; ask(question, conversation, {onToken, onPatch}) sends an `ask` message and resolves with the final `answer`, invoking onToken for each `token` delta and onPatch for each `patch`. Handle inbound tool_call for get_network_logs/get_console_logs by reading AppLens.getStorage().getNetworkRequests()/.getLogs(), shaping compact capped summaries (network: method/url/status/duration; console: level/message/timestamp), and replying with a tool_result keyed by callId. Values are already redacted in storage.

Wire AITab.tsx: on mount probe config.aiAgentURL (AppLens.getConfig()); if set, attempt pair()+connect() with the same iOS-sim/Android-emu(10.0.2.2)/physical-device LAN addressing rules used in OpenAIProvider.buildConnectionHelp. Keep an agentReady ref/state.

In handleSend, when the agent is ready route the question through AgentClient.ask instead of provider.chatStream, streaming token deltas into the SAME streamBufferRef via scheduleFlush/flushStream into the pre-created assistant bubble. When the agent is not ready/unset, call the existing provider.chatStream + ContextEngine path UNCHANGED — strictly no regression.

Render patch messages as a NEW read-only diff bubble: a dedicated bubble that reuses markdownStyles (fence/code_block) to show the unified diff plus the rationale and a Copy button (copyToClipboard). No apply/reject buttons.
Export AgentClient and the shared protocol TYPES from src/index.ts (type-only exports for the protocol message types). Export NOTHING else from src/agent/**.
acceptance_criteria: npm run type-check passes with AgentClient and the AITab wiring in place.
src/agent-client/AgentClient.ts imports no Node-only module and no `ws`; it uses the RN global WebSocket and only type imports from src/agent/protocol.
src/index.ts re-exports exactly AgentClient and shared protocol TYPES and nothing else from src/agent/**.
With aiAgentURL unset or the agent unreachable, AITab uses the existing provider.chatStream + ContextEngine path with identical behavior to today (no regression).
An inbound get_console_logs/get_network_logs tool_call is answered from AppLensStorage with a capped, compact tool_result keyed by callId.
verification: Confirm the RN barrel does not leak Node-only code: inspect dist/index.js / dist/index.d.ts and verify only AgentClient and protocol TYPES appear, with no require of ws or node:fs.
Manual no-regression: with no agent running (aiAgentURL unset), the AI tab streams answers via the existing provider path exactly as before.

Manual round-trip (with FEAT-001 server running against Example/): ask a question that forces a read_file + a get_console_logs call; confirm token deltas stream, the device answers the log tool_call, and a read-only diff bubble renders when propose_patch fires.
findings:
FEAT-002 shipped the RN-safe device half + AITab wiring + barrel exports. For convergence/finalize:

--- New files ---
src/agent-client/AgentClient.ts (RN-safe). Compiles to dist/agent-client/AgentClient.js with ZERO require() calls (all protocol/type imports are `import type`, erased at emit). Uses the RN global WebSocket and fetch only. No `ws`, no node:*.

--- AgentClient public API (now also re-exported) ---
class AgentClient { constructor(baseURL: string, getStorage: () => AppLensStorage); pair(clientInfo?): Promise<PairResponse>; connect(wsUrl: string): Promise<void>; isConnected(): boolean; ask(question, conversation: AIMessage[], handlers?: { onToken?; onPatch? }): Promise<AskResult>; close(): void }. AskResult = { text: string; usage: AIUsage }. The constructor takes a getStorage GETTER (not an instance) so the live buffers are read on each tool_call. One in-flight ask at a time in M1.
  - pair() POSTs /pair and stores the token (token is already embedded in wsUrl per FEAT-001, so connect() opens wsUrl verbatim).
  - Inbound tool_call handling: get_network_logs -> NetworkLogSummary[] (method,url,status,durationMs<-duration,timestamp) from getStorage().getNetworkRequests(); get_console_logs -> ConsoleLogSummary[] (level,message,timestamp) from getStorage().getLogs(). Count arg clamped to [1,200], default 50, newest entries via slice(-count). Replies tool_result keyed by callId. Values already redacted at capture.
  - Routing/correlation: streamed token/patch/answer/error are matched by askId; unknown message types and unparseable frames are ignored (forward-compatible). onclose while a request is in flight rejects it.

--- AITab.tsx wiring ---
- Mount effect probes config.aiAgentURL (AppLens.getConfig()). If set: new AgentClient(resolveAgentURL(url), () => AppLens.getStorage()), then pair()+connect(). Success sets agentClientRef + agentReadyRef=true. ANY failure (unset/unreachable/handshake) leaves agentReadyRef=false and silently falls back. Effect cleanup cancels in-flight pairing and closes the socket; re-runs when config.aiAgentURL changes.
- Platform addressing: adjustLoopbackHost() rewrites //127.0.0.1 or //localhost -> //10.0.2.2 ONLY on Android (emulator), applied to BOTH the base URL and the paired wsUrl. iOS sim / physical-device LAN IPs untouched. Mirrors OpenAIProvider.buildConnectionHelp.
- handleSend: agentClient = agentReadyRef.current ? agentClientRef.current : null. Agent path routes through agentClient.ask streaming into the SAME streamBufferRef via the shared onDelta (scheduleFlush/flushStream) into the pre-created assistant bubble; onPatch appends to a patches[] state. NON-agent path is byte-for-byte today's provider.chatStream + ContextEngine (contextChunks + context summary) — strict no-regression verified.
- Read-only diff bubble: new PatchBubble renders a ```diff fenced block via markdownStyles + path + rationale + a Copy button (copyToClipboard). NO apply/reject (out of scope). FlatList now renders a derived ListItem[] (message | patch) so each patch bubble is interleaved right after its owning assistant message (keyed by assistantId); flatListRef retyped FlatList<ListItem>.
- Note: chatStream returns usage?: AIUsage, so the shared `usage` local is typed `AIUsage | undefined` (unchanged from the original optional assignment into AIMessage.usage).

--- Barrel (src/index.ts) ---
Added `export { AgentClient }` + `export type { AskHandlers, AskResult }` and type-only `export type { DeviceToolName, AskMessage, TokenMessage, PatchMessage, AnswerMessage, ErrorMessage, ToolCallMessage, ToolResultMessage, DeviceToAgentMessage, AgentToDeviceMessage, AgentMessage, NetworkLogSummary, ConsoleLogSummary, PairRequest, PairResponse }` from './agent/protocol'. NOTHING else from src/agent/** is exported.

--- Verification run ---
npm run type-check: clean. npm run build: clean. Barrel leak check: dist/index.js requires only ./agent-client/AgentClient (plus existing core/ai/components) — NO require of ws, node:*, fs, http, crypto, or agent/protocol; dist/agent-client/AgentClient.js has ZERO require() calls; dist/index.d.ts exposes only AgentClient + protocol TYPES. Manual E2E (needs FEAT-001 server + Example app) left to the convergence smoke step.
